meta.note: machine-written (Claude), not reviewed by a native speaker
meta.about: Words the Friuli content uses that Wiktionary lacks (companion/bin/lexicon-build --coverage --lang it lists them): the folklore of Nonno Bepi's stories (sbilfs, krivapete, the Orcolat), Friulian words (fogolâr, pignarûl, cramaro), the region's places as the content names them (the Collio, Cormòns, Carnia, Monte Lussari, Duino, Nova Gorica), the night sky's meteor showers, an imperative with its pronoun joined (arrotolala), the elided c'è, dov'è, cos'è (Wiktionary has them in English only, or as a junk infinitive), and, marked override, a better meaning for suo, whose German through English was sein; n. Each has its meaning in German and Slovene (meanings), so a learner from either reads it in their own language, flagged machine-written. Left out: the people's names (the villagers' come from the cast), the interjections and sounds but eh, the most frequent (hm, shh, bzz), and the wrong choices the dialogs offer on purpose (venirò, vedito).
